---
title: "Random walks"
description-meta: "A random walk on supersingular isogeny graphs, whole, folded by Frobenius, or on the spine."
---

A random walk on a supersingular isogeny graph, with its recent steps highlighted. Choose the graph and the prime $p$ above the picture. The **view** menu shows the whole graph, the graph **folded** by Frobenius (each pair $\{E, E^{(p)}\}$ becomes one vertex, drawn larger, and each edge is an orbit of edges), or only the **spine** (the vertices defined over $\mathbb{F}_p$ and the edges between them). Switch the **animation** to *growing ball* for the [growing-ball animation](balls.qmd).

{{< include /_partials/isogeny-widget.qmd >}}

```{=html}
<script type="module" src="../assets/js/isogeny-hero.js"></script>
```

The level-3 graph has pairs $(E, C)$ with $C$ a subgroup of order 3 as vertices, and a 2-isogeny $\varphi\colon E\to E'$ gives an edge $(E, C)\to(E', \varphi(C))$; the level-5 graph is the same with subgroups of order 5 and both 2- and 3-isogenies. In the spine view some primes are greyed out: for those the spine is empty, for instance the level-3 graph when $p \equiv 1 \pmod 3$. There are pictures of the spines on the [Spines](spines.qmd) page.
